decisive_items: necrotic plaques of the bilateral ears
response.rationale: Acute infection with bacteremia and rapidly progressive symmetric ear necrosis with full-thickness dermal necrosis and sparse inflammation best fits purpura fulminans, a DIC-related syndrome. Septic emboli are less symmetric and typically show more inflammatory response.

rejected.why: Septic emboli usually produce asymmetric distal lesions with more inflammation; bilateral ear necrosis with sparse inflammation is less typical.
Calciphylaxis requires renal failure or calcium-phosphate dysregulation, not present here.
No warfarin use is mentioned; factor VII deficiency does not imply warfarin exposure.
